title: Expression parser gives wrong result for mixed addition and multiplication
prompt: The package in starter/ implements an arithmetic expression parser. tokenizer.py provides tokenize(expr) which splits a string like '3 + 4 * 2' into a list of tokens. parser.py provides parse(tokens) which builds an AST, and eval_ast(node) which evaluates it. The public API in expr.py provides evaluate(expr_str) (one argument) which must continue to work as before (backward compatibility). A new two-argument form evaluate(expr_str, variables) was added to support variable substitution. The expression evaluator gives the wrong result for expressions that mix addition and multiplication — it evaluates left to right without respecting operator precedence, so '3 + 4 * 2' returns 14 instead of 11. All existing single-argument calls must continue to return the same values they did before. The grader tests both the new two-argument form and old single-argument calls including regression tests. Do not edit the tests.
